items.name: Lake Superior
facts: Saint Louis River, Pigeon River, Pic River and others
items.blurb: Lake Superior is a lake in central North America.

items.name: Lake Michigan
facts: Pere Marquette Lake, Dunes Creek, Trail Creek and others
items.blurb: Lake Michigan is one of the five Great Lakes of North America. It is the second-largest of the Great Lakes by volume and depth after Lake Superior and the third-largest by surface area, after Lake Superior and Lake Huron.

items.name: Lake Huron
facts: St. Marys River, Penetangore River, Saugeen River and others
items.blurb: Lake Huron is one of the five Great Lakes of North America. It is shared on the north and east by the Canadian province of Ontario and on the south and west by the U.S. state of Michigan.

items.name: Lake Erie
facts: Detroit River, Maumee River, Sandusky River and others
items.blurb: Lake Erie is the fourth-largest lake by surface area of the five Great Lakes in North America and the eleventh-largest globally. It is the southernmost, shallowest, and smallest by volume of the Great Lakes and also has the shortest average water residence time.

items.name: Lake Ontario
facts: Niagara River, Millhaven Creek, Black River and others
items.blurb: Lake Ontario is one of the five Great Lakes of North America. It is bounded on the north, west, and southwest by the Canadian province of Ontario, and on the south and east by the U.S. state of New York.

items.name: Great Bear Lake
facts: Haldane River, Whitefish River, Johnny Hoe River and others
items.blurb: Great Bear Lake in the boreal forest of Canada is the largest lake entirely in Canada, the fourth-largest in North America, and the eighth-largest in the world.

items.name: Great Slave Lake
facts: Slave River, Tsąkuı Thedá Dezé, Taltson River and others
items.blurb: Great Slave Lake is the second-largest lake in the Northwest Territories, Canada, the deepest lake in North America at 614 m, and the tenth-largest lake in the world by area. It is 469 km long and 20 to 203 km wide.

items.name: Lake Winnipeg
facts: Saskatchewan River, Red River of the North, Winnipeg River and others
items.blurb: Lake Winnipeg is a 24,514-square-kilometre lake in North America, in the Canadian province of Manitoba. Its southern end is about 55 kilometres north of the namesake city, Winnipeg.

items.name: Lake Manitoba
items.blurb: Lake Manitoba is the 14th largest lake in Canada and the 31st largest lake in the world with a total area of 4,624 square kilometres.

items.name: Lake Athabasca
facts: Athabasca River, Fond du Lac River, Grease River and others
items.blurb: Lake Athabasca is in the north-west corner of Saskatchewan and the north-east corner of Alberta between 58° and 60° N in Canada. The lake is about 26% in Alberta and 74% in Saskatchewan.

items.name: Reindeer Lake
items.blurb: Reindeer Lake is a large lake in Western Canada located on the border between north-eastern Saskatchewan and north-western Manitoba. It is the 21st largest lake in the world by area, as well as being the second-largest lake in Saskatchewan and the ninth largest in Canada.

items.name: Lake Nipigon
facts: Namewaminikan River, Whitesand River, Gull River and others
items.blurb: Lake Nipigon is a freshwater lake in Northwestern Ontario. Part of the Great Lakes drainage basin, it drains through the Nipigon River into Lake Superior.

items.name: Great Salt Lake
facts: Jordan River, Bear River, Weber River and others
Its size swings a lot with drought and water use
items.blurb: The Great Salt Lake is the largest saltwater lake in the Western Hemisphere and the eighth-largest terminal lake in the world. It lies in the northern part of the U.S. state of Utah and has a substantial impact upon the local climate, particularly through lake-effect snow.

items.name: Lake Tahoe
facts: Griff Creek, Meeks Creek, Trout Creek and others
items.blurb: Lake Tahoe is a freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada of the Western United States, straddling the border between California and Nevada.

items.name: Lake Okeechobee
items.blurb: Lake Okeechobee is the largest freshwater lake in the U.S. state of Florida.

items.name: Lake Champlain
facts: Otter Creek, Missisquoi River, Winooski River and others
items.blurb: Lake Champlain is a large natural freshwater lake in North America. With a length of 107 mi and surface area over 500 sq mi, it lies mostly between the U.S. states of New York and Vermont, but also extends north into the Canadian province of Quebec.

items.name: Lake Titicaca
facts: Suches River, Ramis River, Coata River and others
items.blurb: Lake Titicaca is a large lake in the Andes mountains on the border of Bolivia and Peru. It is often called the highest navigable lake in the world.

items.name: Lake Poopó
facts: Has almost completely dried up at times
items.blurb: Lake Poopó was a large saline lake in a shallow depression in the Altiplano in Oruro Department, Bolivia, at an altitude of approximately 3,700 m. Due to the lake's length and width, it made up the eastern half of Oruro, known as a mining region in southwest Bolivia.

items.name: Lake Maracaibo
facts: Catatumbo River, Chama River, Apón River and others
A tidal bay-lagoon open to the Caribbean
items.blurb: Lake Maracaibo is located in northwestern Venezuela, between the states of Zulia, Trujillo, and Mérida.

items.name: Lake Argentino
facts: Perito Moreno Glacier, Upsala Glacier, La Leona River
items.blurb: Lago Argentino is a lake in the Patagonian province of Santa Cruz, Argentina. It is the largest freshwater lake in Argentina, with a surface area of 1,415 km2 and a maximum width of 20 mi.

items.name: General Carrera Lake
items.blurb: General Carrera Lake or Lake Buenos Aires is a deep lake located in Patagonia and shared by Argentina and Chile. Both names are internationally accepted, while the autochthonous name of the lake is Chelenko, which means "stormy waters" in Aonikenk.

items.name: Lake Ladoga
items.blurb: Lake Ladoga is a freshwater lake located in the Republic of Karelia and Leningrad Oblast in northwestern Russia, in the vicinity of Saint Petersburg.

items.name: Lake Onega
items.blurb: Lake Onega is a lake in northwestern Russia, on the territory of the Republic of Karelia, Leningrad Oblast and Vologda Oblast. It belongs to the basin of the Baltic Sea, and is the second-largest lake in Europe after Lake Ladoga, slightly smaller than Lebanon.

items.name: Vänern
items.blurb: Vänern is the largest lake in Sweden, the largest lake in the European Union and the third-largest lake in Europe after Ladoga and Onega in Russia. It is located in the provinces of Västergötland, Dalsland, and Värmland in the southwest of the country.

items.name: Vättern
facts: Tabergsån, Huskvarna River, Mjölnaån and others
items.blurb: Vättern is the second-largest lake in Sweden, after Vänern, and the sixth-largest lake in Europe. It is a long, finger-shaped body of fresh water in south central Sweden, to the southeast of Vänern, pointing at the tip of Scandinavia.

items.name: Saimaa
items.blurb: Saimaa is a lake located in the Finnish Lakeland area in southeastern Finland. With a surface area of approximately 4,279 square kilometres, it is the largest lake in Finland, and the fourth-largest natural freshwater lake in Europe.

items.name: Lake Inari
items.blurb: Lake Inari is the largest lake in Sápmi and the third-largest lake in Finland. It is located in the northern part of Lapland, north of the Arctic Circle.

items.name: Lake Peipus
facts: Emajõgi, Velikaya, Võhandu River and others
items.blurb: Lake Peipus is the largest trans-boundary lake in Europe, lying on the international border between Estonia and Russia. The lake is the fifth-largest in Europe after Lake Ladoga and Lake Onega, Lake Vänern, and Lake Saimaa.

items.name: Lake Geneva
facts: Rhône, Dranse, Veveyse River and others
items.blurb: Lake Geneva is a deep lake on the north side of the Alps, shared between Switzerland and France. It is one of the largest lakes in Western Europe and the largest on the course of the Rhône.

items.name: Lake Constance
facts: Rhine, Alter Rhein, Goldach and others
items.blurb: Lake Constance refers to three bodies of water on the Rhine at the northern foot of the Alps: Upper Lake Constance, Lower Lake Constance, and a connecting stretch of the Rhine, called the Seerhein.

items.name: Lake Garda
facts: Sarca, Aril, River Ponale and others
items.blurb: Lake Garda is the largest lake in Italy. It is a popular holiday location in northern Italy, between Brescia and Milan to the west, and Verona and Venice to the east.

items.name: Lake Como
facts: Adda, Albano, Caldone waterfall and others
items.blurb: Lake Como, also known as Lario, is a lake of glacial origin in Lombardy, Italy. It has an area of 146 km2, making it the third-largest lake in Italy, after Lake Garda and Lake Maggiore.

items.name: Loch Ness
facts: River Oich, River Tarff, Caledonian Canal, section between Loch Oich and Loch Ness and others
items.blurb: Loch Ness is a large freshwater loch in the Scottish Highlands. It takes its name from the River Ness, which flows from the northern end.

items.name: Lake Balaton
items.blurb: Lake Balaton is a freshwater rift lake in the Transdanubian region of Hungary. It is the largest lake in Central Europe, and one of the region's foremost tourist destinations.

items.name: Rybinsk Reservoir
items.blurb: Rybinsk Reservoir, informally called the Rybinsk Sea, is a water reservoir on the Volga River and its tributaries the Sheksna and Mologa, formed by Rybinsk Hydroelectric Station dam, located in the Tver, Vologda, and Yaroslavl Oblasts.

items.name: Lake Victoria
facts: Kagera River, Mogusi River, Nyando River and others
items.blurb: Lake Victoria is one of the African Great Lakes.

items.name: Lake Tanganyika
facts: Ruzizi River, Malagarasi River, Kalambo River and others
items.blurb: Lake Tanganyika is an African Great Lake. It is the world's second-largest freshwater lake by volume and the second deepest, in both cases after Lake Baikal in Siberia.

items.name: Lake Malawi
facts: Ruhuhu River, Dwangwa River, Lilongwe River and others
items.blurb: Lake Malawi, also known as Lake Nyasa in Tanzania and Lago Niassa in Mozambique, is an African Great Lake and the southernmost lake in the East African Rift system, located between Malawi, Mozambique and Tanzania.

items.name: Lake Chad
facts: Chari River, Logone River, Yobe River and others
Its area varies hugely between wet and dry seasons
items.blurb: Lake Chad is an endorheic freshwater lake located at the junction of four countries: Nigeria, Niger, Chad, and Cameroon, in western and central Africa respectively, with a catchment area in excess of 1,000,000 km2. It is an important wetland ecosystem in West-Central Africa.

items.name: Lake Turkana
facts: Omo River, Turkwel River, Kibish River and others
items.blurb: Lake Turkana is a saline lake in the Kenyan Rift Valley, predominantly in northern Kenya; the far northern end crosses into Ethiopia. It is the world's largest permanent desert lake and the world's largest alkaline lake.

items.name: Lake Albert
facts: Semliki River, Nkusi River, River Muzizi
items.blurb: Lake Albert, originally known as Lake Mwitanzige by the Banyoro, Nam Ovoyo Bonyo by the Alur, and temporarily as Lake Mobutu Sese Seko, is a lake located in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

items.name: Lake Edward
items.blurb: Lake Edward is one of the smaller African Great Lakes. It is located in the Albertine Rift, the western branch of the East African Rift, on the border between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, with its northern shore a few kilometres south of the equator.

items.name: Lake Kivu
items.blurb: Lake Kivu is one of the African Great Lakes. It lies on the border between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, and is in the Albertine Rift, the western branch of the East African Rift.

items.name: Lake Tana
facts: Lesser Abay River, Reb River, Gumara River and others
Blue Nile, Tana-Beles interbasin water transfer
items.blurb: Lake Tana is the largest lake in Ethiopia and a source of the Blue Nile. Located in Amhara Region in the north-western Ethiopian Highlands, the lake is approximately 84 kilometres long and 66 kilometres wide, with a maximum depth of 15 metres, and an elevation of 1,788 metres.

items.name: Lake Mweru
items.blurb: Lake Mweru is a freshwater lake on the longest arm of Africa's second-longest river, the Congo.

items.name: Lake Kyoga
items.blurb: Lake Kyoga or Lake Kioga is a large shallow lake in Uganda, about 1,720 km2 in area and at an elevation of 1,033 metres. The Victoria Nile flows through the lake on its way from Lake Victoria to Lake Albert.

items.name: Lake Bangweulu
items.blurb: Lake Bangweulu is a freshwater lake in northern Zambia.

items.name: Lake Nasser
items.blurb: Lake Nasser is a large reservoir in southern Egypt and northern Sudan. It was created by the construction of the Aswan High Dam and is one of the largest man-made lakes in the world.

items.name: Lake Volta
facts: White Volta, Oti River, Afram River and others
items.blurb: Lake Volta, the largest artificial reservoir in the world by surface area, is contained behind the Akosombo Dam which generates a substantial amount of Ghana's electricity. It is completely within the country of Ghana and has a surface area of 8,502 square kilometres.

items.name: Lake Kariba
facts: Zambezi River, Sengwa River, Munyati River
items.blurb: Lake Kariba is the world's largest artificial lake and reservoir by volume. It lies 1,300 kilometres upstream from the mouth of the Zambezi river on the Indian Ocean, bordering Zambia and Zimbabwe.

items.name: Lake Baikal
facts: Selenga, Barguzin, Upper Angara and others
items.blurb: Lake Baikal is a rift lake and the deepest lake in the world. It is situated in southern Siberia, Russia, between the federal subjects of Irkutsk Oblast to the northwest and the Republic of Buryatia to the southeast.

items.name: Aral Sea
facts: Once the 4th-largest lake on Earth; it has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s
items.blurb: The Aral Sea was an endorheic salt lake lying between Kazakhstan to its north and Uzbekistan to its south, which began shrinking in the 1950s - 1960s and had largely dried up into desert by 2007. It was in the Aktobe and Kyzylorda regions of Kazakhstan and the Karakalpakstan autonomous region of Uzbekistan.

items.name: Lake Balkhash
facts: Ili River, Aksu River, Ayaguz River and others
items.blurb: Lake Balkhash, also known as Lake Balqash, is a lake in southeastern Kazakhstan. It is one of the largest lakes in Asia and the 15th largest in the world.

items.name: Issyk-Kul
facts: Jyrgalan River, Tamga River, Tosor River and others
items.blurb: Issyk-Kul or Ysyk-Köl is an endorheic saline lake in the western Tian Shan mountains in eastern Kyrgyzstan—just south of a dividing range separating Kyrgyzstan from Kazakhstan.

items.name: Qinghai Lake
items.blurb: Qinghai Lake is the largest lake in China. Located in the Qinghai Province, to which it gave its name, Qinghai Lake is classified as an alkaline endorheic salt lake.

items.name: Dead Sea
facts: Jordan River, Nahal Mishmar, Nahal HaArava and others
Its shore is the lowest land on Earth
items.blurb: The Dead Sea, also known by other names, is a landlocked salt lake bordered by Jordan to the east, the West Bank to the west and Israel to the southwest. It lies in the endorheic basin of the Jordan Rift Valley, and its main tributary is the Jordan River.

items.name: Tonlé Sap
facts: Tonle Sap River, Sangkae River, Chinit River and others
Grows several times larger in the monsoon
items.blurb: Tonle Sap is a lake in central Cambodia. Belonging to the Mekong river system, Tonle Sap is the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia and one of the most diverse and productive ecosystems in the world.

items.name: Lake Urmia
facts: Zarrineh River, Simineh River, Talkheh River and others
Has shrunk drastically in recent decades
items.blurb: Lake Urmia is an endorheic salt lake in Iran. The lake is located in the Iranian region of Azerbaijan, near the Armenian border and south of the Caspian Sea.

items.name: Lake Van
facts: Ankyusner, Bendimahi Brook, Garala and others
items.blurb: Lake Van is the largest lake in Turkey. It lies in the Eastern Anatolia region of Turkey in the provinces of Van and Bitlis, in the Armenian highlands.

items.name: Lake Sevan
items.blurb: Lake Sevan is the largest body of water in Armenia and the broader Caucasus region. It is one of the largest freshwater alpine lakes in Eurasia.

items.name: Lake Khanka
items.blurb: Lake Khanka or Lake Xingkai, is a freshwater lake on the border between Primorsky Krai, Russia and Heilongjiang province, Northeast China.

items.name: Lake Khövsgöl
items.blurb: Lake Khövsgöl, also referred to as Khövsgöl Sea, is a lake in Khövsgöl Province, Mongolia. It is the largest freshwater lake in the country by volume, and the second largest by area after Uvs Lake.

items.name: Poyang Lake
facts: Gan River, Fu River, Le'an River and others
Its area swings widely between seasons
items.blurb: Poyang Lake is the largest freshwater lake in China. Located within Jiujiang Prefecture in Jiangxi Province, it is fed by the Gan, Xin, and Xiu rivers and flows northward into the Yangtze River through a channel.

items.name: Dongting Lake
facts: Yangtze River, Xinqiang He, Zi River and others
items.blurb: Dongting Lake is a large, shallow lake in northeastern Hunan Province, China. Also referred to less frequently as the Dongting Plain, it is a flood basin of the Yangtze River, so its volume depends on the season.

items.name: Lake Tai
items.blurb: Taihu, also known as Lake Tai or Lake Taihu, is a lake in the Yangtze Delta and the third largest freshwater lake in China. The lake is in Jiangsu province and a significant part of its southern shore forms its border with Zhejiang.

items.name: Lake Biwa
facts: Anegawa River, Uso River, Inukami River and others
items.blurb: Lake Biwa is the largest freshwater lake in Japan. It is located entirely within Shiga Prefecture, northeast of the former capital city of Kyoto.

items.name: Lake Toba
items.blurb: Lake Toba is a large natural lake in North Sumatra and Indonesia. The lake is the massive caldera of the Toba supervolcano.

items.name: Lake Eyre
facts: Diamantina River, Warburton River, Cooper Creek and others
Usually a dry salt pan that floods only every few years
items.blurb: Lake Eyre, officially known as Kati Thanda–Lake Eyre, is an endorheic lake in the east-central part of the Far North region of South Australia, some 700 km north of Adelaide.

items.name: Lake Taupō
facts: Waitahanui River, Hinemaiaia Stream, Waiotaka River and others
items.blurb: Lake Taupō is a large crater lake in New Zealand's North Island, located in the caldera of Taupō Volcano. The lake is the namesake of the town of Taupō, which sits on a bay in the lake's northeastern shore.

items.name: Lake Torrens
items.blurb: Lake Torrens is a large ephemeral, normally endorheic salt lake in central South Australia. After sufficiently extreme rainfall events, the lake flows out through the Pirie-Torrens corridor to the Spencer Gulf.
